review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

10:1.sourceText: Σκιὰν γὰρ ἔχων ὁ νόμος τῶν μελλόντων ἀγαθῶν, οὐκ αὐτὴν τὴν εἰκόνα τῶν πραγμάτων, κατ’ ἐνιαυτὸν ταῖς αὐταῖς θυσίαις ἃς προσφέρουσιν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς οὐδέποτε δύναται τοὺς προσερχομένους τελειῶσαι·
10:1.targetText: For the Law having a shadow of the good things coming—not the very image of the matters, every year, by the same sacrifices that they offer continually, is never able to make perfect those coming near,

groups.note: The actual εἰς τὸ διηνεκές is the complete continually/continuously adverbial phrase; English expresses its preposition/article/continuous constituent once as continually.

10:2.sourceText: ἐπεὶ οὐκ ἂν ἐπαύσαντο προσφερόμεναι, διὰ τὸ μηδεμίαν ἔχειν ἔτι συνείδησιν ἁμαρτιῶν τοὺς λατρεύοντας ἅπαξ κεκαθαρισμένους;
10:2.targetText: since, would they not have ceased to be offered, because of those serving having no more conscience of sins, having been purified once?

groups.note: The actual present passive feminine-plural offering participle agrees with the sacrifices ceasing; English recasts that same offered-action relation as the infinitive to be offered, without a separately printed infinitive form.
The actual διά with its articular infinitival clause marks the causal reason; English because of expresses that construction without an independent second of word.

10:3.sourceText: ἀλλ’ ἐν αὐταῖς ἀνάμνησις ἁμαρτιῶν κατ’ ἐνιαυτόν·
10:3.targetText: But in those [sacrifices] is a remembrance of sins every year,

unmappedTarget.reason: English explicitly repeats the antecedent sacrifices with those; pinned N1904 has the personal/anaphoric αὐταῖς without a written sacrifice noun in this clause.
English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

10:4.sourceText: ἀδύνατον γὰρ αἷμα ταύρων καὶ τράγων ἀφαιρεῖν ἁμαρτίας.
10:4.targetText: for it is impossible for blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

groups.note: The actual accusative blood noun is the subject of the take-away infinitive; English for blood states that same infinitival-subject relation without a separately written Greek for.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

10:5.sourceText: Διὸ εἰσερχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον λέγει Θυσίαν καὶ προσφορὰν οὐκ ἠθέλησας, σῶμα δὲ κατηρτίσω μοι·
10:5.targetText: For this reason, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering You did not will, and a body You prepared for Me;

groups.note: The actual θέλω predicate is volitional, You did will/want, not a future auxiliary.

10:6.sourceText: ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας οὐκ εὐδόκησας.
10:6.targetText: in burnt-offerings, and concerning sin-offerings, You did not delight.

groups.note: The actual περὶ ἁμαρτίας sacrificial formula contains the sin noun and its concerning preposition; LSV names the understood sin-offerings. The actual source sin head remains visible, without inventing a separately printed offering noun or changing singular sin into a Greek plural.

The actual εὐδοκέω delight/approve verb governs the offering objects; English expresses its object relation with delight in, placing in before burnt-offerings. That English in belongs to this verb-complement recast, not an independently printed Greek ἐν.

10:7.sourceText: τότε εἶπον Ἰδοὺ ἥκω, ἐν κεφαλίδι βιβλίου γέγραπται περὶ ἐμοῦ, τοῦ ποιῆσαι ὁ Θεός, τὸ θέλημά σου.
10:7.targetText: Then I said, Behold, I come (in a volume of the scroll it has been written concerning Me), to do, O God, Your will”;

groups.note: The actual nominative God with article functions as direct address; English O marks that real address construction without an independent Greek O particle.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

10:8.sourceText: ἀνώτερον λέγων ὅτι Θυσίας καὶ προσφορὰς καὶ ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας οὐκ ἠθέλησας οὐδὲ εὐδόκησας, αἵτινες κατὰ νόμον προσφέρονται,
10:8.targetText: saying above, “Sacrifice, and offering, and burnt-offerings, and concerning sin-offering You did not will, nor delight in” (which are offered according to the Law),

groups.note: The actual θυσίας is plural sacrifices; LSV uses the singular collective Sacrifice.
The actual προσφοράς is plural offerings; LSV uses the singular collective offering.

The actual περὶ ἁμαρτίας sin-concerning sacrificial formula is rendered concerning sin-offering. No separately written offering noun is supplied in the source; the actual sin lemma is preserved under this contextual designation.

The actual second-person finite delight predicate is coordinated with did-will; English shares the earlier You did auxiliary and supplies the in complement relation. The same real delight head remains distinct from the separate wanting verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual reporting ὅτι introduces the quotation; English gives the direct quote without another that.

10:9.sourceText: τότε εἴρηκεν Ἰδοὺ ἥκω τοῦ ποιῆσαι τὸ θέλημά σου. ἀναιρεῖ τὸ πρῶτον ἵνα τὸ δεύτερον στήσῃ.
10:9.targetText: then He said, “Behold, I come to do, O God, Your will”; He takes away the first that He may establish the second;

groups.note: The actual εἴρηκεν is perfect has said; LSV uses simple past He said with the same actual saying head.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: The longer witness repeats the divine address ὁ Θεός; pinned N1904 has no God noun or address here.

10:10.sourceText: ἐν ᾧ θελήματι ἡγιασμένοι ἐσμὲν διὰ τῆς προσφορᾶς τοῦ σώματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐφάπαξ.
10:10.targetText: in which will, we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all,

groups.note: The actual perfect passive sanctified participle with present we-are auxiliary forms the written periphrastic perfect. The English complete we-have-been-sanctified predicate retains both actual verbal forms.
The explicit ἐφάπαξ adverb supplies once for all, independently of the sanctified predicate tense. Its scope is not inferred merely from a Greek aorist/perfect form.

10:11.sourceText: Καὶ πᾶς μὲν ἱερεὺς ἕστηκεν καθ’ ἡμέραν λειτουργῶν καὶ τὰς αὐτὰς πολλάκις προσφέρων θυσίας, αἵτινες οὐδέποτε δύνανται περιελεῖν ἁμαρτίας·
10:11.targetText: and every priest, indeed, has daily stood serving, and offering the same sacrifices many times, that are never able to take away sins.

10:12.sourceText: οὗτος δὲ μίαν ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν προσενέγκας θυσίαν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ Θεοῦ,
10:12.targetText: But He, having offered one sacrifice for sin—to the end, sat down at the right hand of God—

groups.note: The actual ἁμαρτιῶν is plural sins, expressed by English collective singular sin; the actual ethical sin head is retained.

The actual εἰς τὸ διηνεκές is the continuously/perpetually adverbial phrase. LSV to the end expresses its enduring extension; the source has no separate τέλος end noun. This note preserves the wording without deciding the attachment of this phrase to the offering or the sitting.
Actual genitive article and God noun jointly supply of God as the right-hand qualifier. The distinct offering/sitting and duration constituents remain unchanged.

10:13.sourceText: τὸ λοιπὸν ἐκδεχόμενος ἕως τεθῶσιν οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτοῦ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ.
10:13.targetText: as to the rest, expecting until He may place His enemies [as] His footstool,

groups.note: The actual τὸ λοιπόν is the for-the-remainder/henceforth adverbial construction, rendered as to the rest as a whole phrase.

Pinned τεθῶσιν is passive third-person plural may be placed, with the enemies as grammatical subject. LSV recasts the actual placement head as active may place; its explicit personal agent He remains separately explained rather than invented from the passive.

The actual footstool-of-the-feet constituent is compressed into English footstool, with as expressing its predicate-complement role under placing. The explicit Greek feet designation and footstool remain the same shared constituent; no unrelated under-feet preposition or new as token is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names a personal agent for the placement, whereas pinned N1904 has a passive plural enemies-may-be-placed predicate without a written agent pronoun. The tag alone does not identify or print that agent.

10:14.sourceText: μιᾷ γὰρ προσφορᾷ τετελείωκεν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς τοὺς ἁγιαζομένους.
10:14.targetText: for by one offering He has perfected to the end those being sanctified;

groups.note: The actual εἰς τὸ διηνεκές expresses continuously/perpetually; LSV to the end is the same complete adverbial constituent rather than a separately written Greek end noun.

10:15.sourceText: Μαρτυρεῖ δὲ ἡμῖν καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον· μετὰ γὰρ τὸ εἰρηκέναι
10:15.targetText: and the Holy Spirit also testifies to us, for after that He has said before,

groups.note: The actual article plus perfect saying infinitive is the content after which the next testimony follows; English recasts it as that He has said. The real perfect saying head is retained without a written finite form or a free source that conjunction.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness prefix difference: LSV follows προειρηκέναι, to have said beforehand; pinned N1904 has plain εἰρηκέναι, to have said, without the before prefix.

10:16.sourceText: Αὕτη ἡ διαθήκη ἣν διαθήσομαι πρὸς αὐτοὺς μετὰ τὰς ἡμέρας ἐκείνας, λέγει Κύριος· διδοὺς νόμους μου ἐπὶ καρδίας αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν διάνοιαν αὐτῶν ἐπιγράψω αὐτούς,
10:16.targetText: “This [is] the covenant that I will make with them after those days, says the LORD, giving My laws on their hearts, and I will write them on their minds,”

groups.note: The actual διάνοιαν mind noun is singular; English uses plural minds with the collective people. Its same understanding/mind head is retained with the number recast explicit.

The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

10:17.targetText: and, “I will remember their sins and their lawlessness no more”;

groups.note: The actual plural ἀνομίαι is rendered collective singular lawlessness; its own lawlessness head remains distinct from the preceding sins noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

10:18.sourceText: ὅπου δὲ ἄφεσις τούτων, οὐκέτι προσφορὰ περὶ ἁμαρτίας.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

10:19.sourceText: Ἔχοντες οὖν, ἀδελφοί, παρρησίαν εἰς τὴν εἴσοδον τῶν ἁγίων ἐν τῷ αἵματι Ἰησοῦ,
10:19.targetText: Having, therefore, brothers, boldness for the entrance into the holy places, by the blood of Jesus,

groups.note: The actual genitive holy-places phrase specifies the sanctuary destination of entrance. English into the holy places states that same entry-goal relationship without another written Greek into preposition.

10:20.sourceText: ἣν ἐνεκαίνισεν ἡμῖν ὁδὸν πρόσφατον καὶ ζῶσαν διὰ τοῦ καταπετάσματος, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ,
10:20.targetText: which [is] the way He initiated for us—new and living, through the veil, that is, His flesh—

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English inserts a copula in which is the way to recast the appositional way object. The source has no be verb there; its actual later ἔστιν belongs to that is His flesh.

10:21.sourceText: καὶ ἱερέα μέγαν ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Θεοῦ,
10:21.targetText: and a Great Priest over the house of God,

groups.note: Actual genitive article and God noun jointly supply of God as the house qualifier; no independent Greek of preposition is printed.

10:22.sourceText: προσερχώμεθα μετὰ ἀληθινῆς καρδίας ἐν πληροφορίᾳ πίστεως, ῥεραντισμένοι τὰς καρδίας ἀπὸ συνειδήσεως πονηρᾶς καὶ λελουσμένοι τὸ σῶμα ὕδατι καθαρῷ·
10:22.targetText: may we draw near with a true heart, in full assurance of faith, having the hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and having the body bathed with pure water;

groups.note: The actual perfect passive ῥεραντισμένοι describes us as sprinkled, with hearts as the respect/body-part accusative. LSV recasts that state as having the hearts sprinkled; having is English result-state framing, not a separately written active having verb or a different original sprinkling head.

The actual perfect middle/passive washed participle describes the people with respect to the body. English having the body bathed recasts that same washing/body state, without an independently written Greek have verb.

10:23.sourceText: κατέχωμεν τὴν ὁμολογίαν τῆς ἐλπίδος ἀκλινῆ, πιστὸς γὰρ ὁ ἐπαγγειλάμενος,
10:23.targetText: may we hold fast the unwavering profession of the hope (for He who promised [is] faithful),

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

10:24.sourceText: καὶ κατανοῶμεν ἀλλήλους εἰς παροξυσμὸν ἀγάπης καὶ καλῶν ἔργων,
10:24.targetText: and may we consider to provoke one another to love and to good works,

groups.note: The actual reciprocal is the direct object of considering one another; English places that same immediately considered-and-provoked participant as object of provoke. The shared people remain actual under this local construction recast, not a new pronoun or unrelated participant.
The actual εἰς παροξυσμόν is for a provocation/stirring-up. English verbalizes that purpose-noun constituent as to provoke; the written source head remains παροξυσμός, not an invented παροξύνω verb.
The actual genitive works is coordinated with love as the stirring-up content; English to good works states that same intended-content relation without a separately written to preposition.

10:25.sourceText: μὴ ἐγκαταλείποντες τὴν ἐπισυναγωγὴν ἑαυτῶν, καθὼς ἔθος τισίν, ἀλλὰ παρακαλοῦντες, καὶ τοσούτῳ μᾶλλον ὅσῳ βλέπετε ἐγγίζουσαν τὴν ἡμέραν.
10:25.targetText: not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as [is] a custom of some, but exhorting, and so much the more as you see the Day coming near.

groups.note: The actual dative indefinite pronoun specifies the people for whom this is customary; English expresses that custom/people relation as of some without changing the source to a genitive.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

10:26.sourceText: Ἑκουσίως γὰρ ἁμαρτανόντων ἡμῶν μετὰ τὸ λαβεῖν τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν τῆς ἀληθείας, οὐκέτι περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ἀπολείπεται θυσία,
10:26.targetText: For [if] we are sinning willingly after receiving the full knowledge of the truth—there remains no more sacrifice for sins,

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a conditional frame for the we-sinning genitive-absolute circumstance. The context determines its conditional force; pinned Greek has no separately written if particle in this clause.

10:27.sourceText: φοβερὰ δέ τις ἐκδοχὴ κρίσεως καὶ πυρὸς ζῆλος ἐσθίειν μέλλοντος τοὺς ὑπεναντίους.
10:27.targetText: but a certain fearful looking for of judgment, and fiery zeal, about to devour the opposers;

groups.note: The actual genitive fire noun qualifies zeal, zeal of fire; English recasts this as the adjective fiery without an independently written Greek fiery adjective.

The actual genitive about-to participle agrees with fire in zeal-of-fire-about-to-devour. English attaches the same devouring prospect to fiery zeal as its nominal phrase; no different written nominative participle is claimed.

10:28.sourceText: ἀθετήσας τις νόμον Μωϋσέως χωρὶς οἰκτιρμῶν ἐπὶ δυσὶν ἢ τρισὶν μάρτυσιν ἀποθνήσκει·
10:28.targetText: anyone having set aside a law of Moses dies without mercies on the basis of two or three witnesses.

10:29.sourceText: πόσῳ δοκεῖτε χείρονος ἀξιωθήσεται τιμωρίας ὁ τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ καταπατήσας καὶ τὸ αἷμα τῆς διαθήκης κοινὸν ἡγησάμενος ἐν ᾧ ἡγιάσθη, καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα τῆς χάριτος ἐνυβρίσας.
10:29.targetText: Of how much worse punishment will he be counted worthy who trampled on the Son of God, and counted the blood of the covenant a common thing, by which he was sanctified, and having insulted the Spirit of grace?

groups.note: The actual genitive punishment gives what the offender is counted worthy of; English fronts that same genitive relation as Of how much worse punishment.
Actual genitive article and God noun jointly supply of God as the Son qualifier. The separate covenant and grace genitives retain their own actual nominal heads.
The actual common adjective is a predicate description of blood; English a common thing supplies nominal support for that same predicate rather than an independently written generic thing noun.
Actual genitive article and grace noun jointly supply of ... grace as the Spirit qualifier. The preceding separate God and covenant constructions remain distinct.

unmappedSource.reason: Pinned δοκεῖτε explicitly asks you think/suppose within the question; LSV omits this parenthetical thinking predicate.

10:30.sourceText: οἴδαμεν γὰρ τὸν εἰπόντα Ἐμοὶ ἐκδίκησις, ἐγὼ ἀνταποδώσω· καὶ πάλιν Κρινεῖ Κύριος τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ.
10:30.targetText: For we have known Him who is saying, “Vengeance [is] Mine, I will repay, says the LORD”; and again, “The LORD will judge His people.”

groups.note: Pinned εἰπόντα is an aorist saying participle, the one who said; LSV uses present is saying. The same speaking predicate is retained with that tense/form recast explicit.
The actual dative ἐμοί gives the to-Me possession/assignment relation for vengeance; English Mine states that same first-person entitlement rather than a different written Greek possessive form.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

The longer witness inserts λέγει κύριος after I will repay; pinned N1904 has no saying predicate or LORD title at that quotation position. The actual later LORD belongs to the second quotation and is not borrowed here.

10:31.targetText: [It is] fearful to fall into [the] hands of [the] living God.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.
English supplies an article with the hands phrase; the actual Greek hands noun is anarthrous.

10:32.sourceText: Ἀναμιμνῄσκεσθε δὲ τὰς πρότερον ἡμέρας, ἐν αἷς φωτισθέντες πολλὴν ἄθλησιν ὑπεμείνατε παθημάτων,
10:32.targetText: But call to your remembrance the former days, in which, having been enlightened, you endured much conflict of sufferings;

groups.note: The actual second-person middle remember/recall imperative is expanded as call to your remembrance. Your realizes its addressed-person/self-recollection relation, not a separately written Greek possessive or remembrance noun.

10:33.sourceText: τοῦτο μὲν ὀνειδισμοῖς τε καὶ θλίψεσιν θεατριζόμενοι, τοῦτο δὲ κοινωνοὶ τῶν οὕτως ἀναστρεφομένων γενηθέντες.
10:33.targetText: this indeed, being made spectacles with both insults and afflictions, now this, having become partners of those so living,

groups.note: The paired τοῦτο μὲν ... τοῦτο δέ divides the suffering account into two respects, partly this/partly that. English now this expresses the second contrasting aspect; now is not a separately written temporal νῦν.
The actual middle conduct/lifestyle participle ἀναστρεφομένων describes those living/conducting themselves in this way; it is not the different Greek life verb ζάω.

10:34.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ τοῖς δεσμίοις συνεπαθήσατε, καὶ τὴν ἁρπαγὴν τῶν ὑπαρχόντων ὑμῶν μετὰ χαρᾶς προσεδέξασθε, γινώσκοντες ἔχειν ἑαυτοὺς κρείσσονα ὕπαρξιν καὶ μένουσαν.
10:34.targetText: for you also sympathized with my bonds, and the robbery of your goods you received with joy, knowing that you have in yourselves a better substance in the heavens, and an enduring one.

groups.note: Actual genitive article and substantival present active having/existing participle jointly supply of ... goods as the robbery complement. Both raw analyses retain V-PAP-GPN for the actual hyparcho head; your remains separately linked to its real genitive pronoun. The actual substantive having/existing participle names possessions/things belonging, rendered goods. The written head remains ὑπάρχω, not a different original goods noun.
The actual having infinitive is the content of knowing; English finite that-you-have states that same content clause without an independently written that conjunction.

Pinned accusative ἑαυτούς is the personal subject of the having infinitive, yourselves as possessors. English realizes the same people as you in that you have. The added in-yourselves relation follows a different dative/preposition reading and is separately explained.

The actual ὕπαρξις denotes possession/property, rendered substance; the same actual possession is resumed by English one in an enduring one. It is not a claim that a separate Greek one numeral or material-substance noun is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness lexical difference: pinned τοῖς δεσμίοις identifies prisoners, while LSV my bonds follows TR τοῖς δεσμοῖς μου, chains with a first-person possessor. The persons noun and chains noun are not the same lexical head.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness lexical difference: LSV follows the chains-and-my-possessor reading; pinned N1904 names prisoners in the dative without a my pronoun. The actual prisoner identity is not relabeled as bonds.

Source-witness case/attachment difference: LSV follows an in-yourselves expression, while pinned N1904 has accusative yourselves as the subject of have. The reflexive subject is not transferred to an inward-location phrase.
The longer witness adds the heavenly location ἐν οὐρανοῖς; pinned N1904 has no heaven name or location phrase here.

10:35.sourceText: Μὴ ἀποβάλητε οὖν τὴν παρρησίαν ὑμῶν, ἥτις ἔχει μεγάλην μισθαποδοσίαν.
10:35.targetText: You may not cast away, then, your boldness, which has great repayment of reward,

groups.note: The actual recompense noun μισθαποδοσία contains the reward/payment sense, rendered repayment of reward as a whole expression without independently printed repayment and reward nouns.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

10:36.sourceText: ὑπομονῆς γὰρ ἔχετε χρείαν ἵνα τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ ποιήσαντες κομίσησθε τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν.
10:36.targetText: for you have need of patience, that having done the will of God, you may receive the promise.

groups.note: Actual genitive article and God noun jointly supply of God as the will qualifier. The actual will noun and doing participle remain separately linked.

10:37.sourceText: ἔτι γὰρ μικρὸν ὅσον ὅσον, ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἥξει καὶ οὐ χρονίσει·
10:37.targetText: “For yet [in] a very, very little [while], He who is coming will come, and will not linger,”

groups.note: The actual μικρὸν ὅσον ὅσον is an intensified very-little-while idiom. English in and while make its temporal extent explicit within that whole written construction, not separate Greek preposition/time-noun tokens.

10:38.sourceText: ὁ δὲ δίκαιός μου ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται, καὶ ἐὰν ὑποστείληται, οὐκ εὐδοκεῖ ἡ ψυχή μου ἐν αὐτῷ.
10:38.targetText: but, “The righteous will live by faith; and if he may draw back, My soul has no pleasure in him.”

unmappedSource.reason: Pinned μου qualifies the righteous person as My righteous one; LSV does not express that first-person possessor. It is not borrowed for the later separate My soul phrase, which has its own actual μου.
The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

10:39.sourceText: ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑποστολῆς εἰς ἀπώλειαν, ἀλλὰ πίστεως εἰς περιποίησιν ψυχῆς.
10:39.targetText: But we are not of those drawing back to destruction, but of those believing to a preserving of soul.

groups.note: The actual genitive ὑποστολῆς is the abstract withdrawal/shrinking-back noun describing a class/characterization of people. English personalizes that relation as of those drawing back; the actual source lemma remains the withdrawal noun, not a written withdrawing verb or those pronoun.

The actual genitive πίστεως is the faith noun in the opposed characterization. English expresses that faith class personally as of those believing; this retains the actual faith head, not an invented πιστεύω participle or separate source those pronoun.
